ops.text: The user wants to know how session expiry works. The store lives in src/session/ — I should read the store and the sweeper before answering, and check whether expiry is lazy or scheduled.

ops.name: grep
ops.intent: Find where expiry is read and written

ops.name: read
read

ops.text:
Expiry is handled in two places, and both are needed:

1. **Lazily on read.** `SessionStore.get()` compares `expiresAt` with the injected clock and deletes the entry before returning `undefined`. An expired session can never be served, even if the sweeper is late.
2. **Periodically by the sweeper.** `startSweeper()` walks the map every 60 s and removes expired entries, so sessions that are never read again do not leak memory.

```ts
if (entry.expiresAt <= now) {
  this.entries.delete(id);
  return undefined;
}
```

| Path | Trigger | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `get()` | every read | correctness |
| `sweep()` | every 60 s | memory |

One thing worth changing: `touch()` always extends `expiresAt`, so a client that polls keeps its session alive forever. If you want an absolute lifetime, store `createdAt` and cap the extension.
